a.text: Skadi watches as the locals fall unconscious, and she picks up the suitcase she'd laid for a second on the floor.

steps.text: ...Gr—Greetings.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hm? There's another one.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Don't—Don't hit me... I'm not very much like them. I know you're good.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You can understand what I mean.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You only came here following Bench.

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: *Whimper*... Woodframe, Woodframe...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: He ran, I followed.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You bear no ill will towards us.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: All I ask is he gives what's mine back.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: B—Bench... what did you take?

steps.name: Young Inhabitant
steps.text: All shiny... all shiny... hard... it hurts... *whimper*...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: That's not for you to eat! Pull it out of your mouth, quick!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I'm sorry, Bench tends to just grab at things he's never seen before. He doesn't understand these are things he shouldn't grab.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Receives necklace)

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Ugh, it's covered in spit... It's gotten your hand dirty.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's fine, as long as I have it back.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: We don't often see unfamiliar faces here. Did you come from the outside?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I came from a city elsewhere in Iberia.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: It's very rare I see people from other places.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Your clothes... are very strange too. I've never seen material like this before. Does everyone from the outside dress that way?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Only wandering singers would.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Wandering... singers? I overheard you talking to Sheetmetal, but I don't know what that is.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Like me, they travel everywhere, occasionally stopping over, playing the harp, singing a song.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: What about the case? What's inside it?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: A saxophone.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: What's a saxophone?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: An instrument.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Are you really a wandering singer?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Mm.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: (Quiet mutter)

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: So what did you come to do, then? Was it sing?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I came to find someone.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Who? Also a wandering singer?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes. She is a fellow of mine. We are colleagues.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Did she come to Sal Viento too?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Correct. Have you seen her?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You haven't told me what she looks like yet... oh, well! I said it just before, but you're the first time I've ever seen anyone like you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'll go and ask others. Can you guide me?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Guide? That trap... was my making. I thought you would've known.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't care.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You don't fault me? I thought you would at least have... reproached me some.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Let's go. I'm in a hurry.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Agh!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Why—Why did you suddenly stop...? I knocked against your case. Ow...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I forgot to say. What's in my case is useless to you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Apart from this, anything you might want, I can give you once you help me find her.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Er, I was only curious... Was I that apparent?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: As plain to see as the trap you made.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Wow... singer, you not only have a pair of nimble hands, but a pair of formidable eyes too.

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Ninety-eight...

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Ninety-nine...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: How do I ask questions here?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Huh? How do you usually ask them on the outside?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (With a thump, she sets down the case she was carrying.)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: With this.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Um? The saxo... saxophone? You use instruments to ask questions?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Slam slam, boom, kapow.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: The sounds this instrument makes are quite bizarre.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's very effective. They all usually open up straight away.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If they still don't talk, I can change angle, and go for another round.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Then I have a feeling that won't get you anywhere here.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Possibly.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Strokes case)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: In that case, the two just now. They already got talking.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Sheetmetal? They shouldn't even know of musical instruments. The people here usually keep themselves to themselves, and don't pay attention to anyone.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: And they, er, talk very infrequently. Even if they knew, they wouldn't understand how to reply.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You've paid attention to me.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Probably because I'm a little odd. I'm not too like everyone else.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You talk a lot better than they do too.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Do I really? I'm so happy. It's all what Grandma Petra taught me.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh, if you want to find someone else to ask, I can bring you to Grandma Petra. She's the oldest one of us all here, and knows about the most too.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Come, singer, let us walk through here.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Here?

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Ninety-nine, ninety-nine...

steps.name: Inhabitant
steps.text: Ninety-nine.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Do you mean them? You can ignore them, they're just standing around. They make it a bit of a squeeze, but it'll be alright even if you bump into them. They won't react, really. Will you, Tableleg?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Wha? She jumped—clear over their heads? H—How did she manage that? She didn't so much as touch anyone beneath her.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Do all people from the outside walk about like this? How magical!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Made it!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma Petra! Graaaandmaaaa Petraaaa!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Don't shout! Are you trying to shake my ears apart?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Hee-hee, grandma, you're so very lively today! You're still—er, are you basking in the sun?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: The sun... keh, where do you see the sun? I've been waiting all these years and I still haven't seen the sun. Anita, what are you getting up to? You're always scrambling about, doing this and that.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Around here, could anything important even happen?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma Petra, I'm fine as I am. Someone else wanted to find you.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: —Huh, where'd she go?

a.text: Skadi stares fixed at the alley's other end.
There's no one to be seen there. At least, it seems so.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: How did you get over here all of a sudden?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Someone's watching.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: That so? Where? I can't see anyone around.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They're hiding very well. Not well enough, is all.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Why are you so grim? Aren't you a wandering singer? Shouldn't you be very used to people staring if you perform?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...You're right.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Then let's make our way over! Grandma Petra's in alright spirits. You might really be able to ask something or other.

a.text: At a street corner, an old lady rounds a pillar, turning circle after circle.
Her body trembles and shakes, yet her gait is no hobble.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Red sky at night, set aglow by my fiery clothes... beloved one, o, take me to fly o'er the deep blue ocean...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma Petra, what are you doing now?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Anita, oh, curse you, Anita! Did you not see I was dancing?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: When a young girl is dancing, nobody can disturb her. Are you going to dance along with me, Anita?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I... I don't know how.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Spin a little slower. Watch you don't make yourself dizzy again.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Nonsense! How would I go dizzy? I could round it ten and some times, and the whole city would clap for me!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: I... *cough* *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Take a little break. Look, we have a wandering singer here. She has a question to ask you.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: A wandering singer? I've never seen any wandering singer in my good long years.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: This sunlight... this sunlight's carried on far too long. Why hasn't night come yet? Once the sun's turned in, there'll be people playing away in the bar... Will you be playing in there too?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: We dance in the square, yes, right here we do... oh, I could spin more times than you could count. I have a red skirt, girlie, and I must say, it's much more beautiful than the one you're wearing.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: So many youngsters want to dance with me. I like Manuel the most out of all of them. He was the most handsome when he was young.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Yes, Grandma Petra, you've told me this. You've told me plenty of times now.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Besides, who's looking for me?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Is it you? Your red dress is so pretty.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Red... no, I don't want... I don't want one red.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: The seawater! The seawater is alive!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh, no, here it goes again...

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: ...suddenly came washing up. Everyone dead! All so fine... so many fine people. The survivors had nothing either to eat.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Manuel... Manuel told me he'd take me with him. Then he went back on that. He said all those people who left had never come back. All of them had died on the outside.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You've told me this before as well.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: And then he said he'd protect me. He promised me—he said he'd protect me! But he only wanted to make a fool of me—

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: He wanted to swindle me out of all the food I'd kept—*cough* *cough*, I pretended to agree, and I took the silver vase my mother left behind—*cough* *cough* *cough* *cough*—

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Red... I like red... no, I don't want...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma Petra, Grandma Petra! Just leave it, okay? You always get out of breath once you start going on about this.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: The one I brought to see you today wanted to ask about something else.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Ask? Who's asking?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Her. A wandering singer from the outside.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Tell her who you're looking for, quickly! While Grandma Petra still has the strength to answer.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hello—

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Who're you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: A wandering singer. I'm searching for someone just like me, come from the outside as well.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: An out—An outsider! You're pulling my leg!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: No outsider would ever come around these parts, they stopped caring about us long ago...

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: You came to steal something, didn't you? You're going to steal my food, my clothes, you're going to sup on my flesh, drink my blood—

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Monster! You're a monster!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Frowns)

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma, there isn't a monster. She's just a wandering singer.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Red hem... red... I've found one, here... the singing has arisen... Manuel is waiting for me, I must go, I should go...

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Beloved one, o, set aglow by my fiery clothes... fiery clothes...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I'm sorry, Grandma Petra's particularly worked up today. Maybe I shouldn't have brought you to see her.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I'll take her back inside, singer. Give me a moment.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Singer, are you still looking for the one watching you?

a.text: Across the opposite corner, a dark shadow stows away in an even deeper cloud's gloom.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Lurking trouble is like a beastling too scared to bare its fangs. No need to care.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma Petra was...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She knows of playing instruments, and knows to dance. The way she spoke was akin to an outsider.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Really? No wonder. She speaks of so much, I can't make heads or tails of it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She called me a monster.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: She didn't mean to. Grandma often sees things that aren't real. It's like she's dreaming all the time.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Who isn't.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: She's taken ill. She can't answer your question now.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: A shame.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Don't be worried.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: There are other brothers of mine where I live. I can take you to ask them in a while. I'm just not sure if they'll be willing to open up. Sometimes it really is so hard to speak with them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Brothers?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Yes, brothers. You're an Iberian too. Don't you call them so?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: My mother had no other children—but—I have very many brothers and sisters. In this town, we are all brothers and sisters. That's what the laws say.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: And you believe in those.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: What else would we do? When I was very young, Grandma Petra even told me that in those dark days past, we had made mistakes.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: In those times, each one of us only looked after ourselves, hiding in each home, never speaking. Sometimes a can would be dug out, and we would, um, fight over it.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Then things gradually got better. Now we'll live together, and occasionally talk. Everyone's started to, erm—learn to share.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: —'We want to survive, so we must love one another even more. For love is the inseparable bond between us. We may not steal, we may not fight.'

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: 'Make oneself sturdy, but our whole self sturdier still. Only this way will bring a better life.'

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: This sounds familiar.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Really? The priest says everyone from the outside believes this too.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I forgot to say, the priest taught us this!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: He'll tell us so much every time... most of it is lost on me. Apart from those few words just now, all I remember is we need to treat each other as brothers, and be a little kinder to each other. I suppose it is nice advice, isn't it?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Priest?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Yes. Just like you, he came from the outside too. Though that was very many years ago.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: It was ever since he came that things improved. He's a brother among us.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Is he alone?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Most of the time he's alone. Oh, I heard from Sheetmetal's friends there was one more too, later on.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I've never seen her. She doesn't seem to show herself. Occasionally when the priest is speaking to us, she'll be standing behind him. I only ever see that one glimpse of her from far away.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Why are you... in such a hurry suddenly? Do you need to go somewhere?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm going to the chapel.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Do you know how to get there?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Your chapel isn't that hard to recognize.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: The way there's not so easy. You need to follow the coast from here. Come, let me show you.

a.text: The girl leads Skadi along a lengthy stretch of path.
The two gradually near the shore, the chapel roof always somehow in their sight, yet still far away as ever.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Why did you stop?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: So they followed.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: What do you mean? You've lost me again.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: That clingy beastling.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: That's strange. You keep saying beastling—that should be an animal, right? We've got no animals living here—they disappeared long ago!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's fine. Let's keep going.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Very well, friend from the outside. You're in charge.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: What did you see? It's right there.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: But we don't usually go to the chapel at this time.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I have ways in.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You can enter, we all can. The chapel's entrance is forever open to the devout—the priest said so. But... you wanted to seek someone out, didn't you?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: He isn't usually in the chapel at this time.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What times is he in?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Every so often, he'll appear before us of his own accord, and make friendly conversation with every one of us.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: If you have any issues, those are also times you can go find him. No matter what it is that bothers you, he'll never reject you.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: On such days, until the sun rises the next morning, he'll be in the chapel waiting.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: That's right, he can also help you in your search! I'm sure the priest would know much more than any of us!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: How long is 'every so often?'

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Um, I haven't seen him in the recent while. I'm not like them—I don't really count the days. But it should be the next two days? All our food is about to run bare.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Strange. Whenever you say alright, I always feel like it isn't a sincere reply.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: No, that's wrong of me. The priest said, we shouldn't doubt others. Ugh, they all say I'm so fond of thinking of all these questions, and it won't help me lead a good life in any way.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Were those also his words?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Haha, he'd never tell me this. I'd slip off before he knew it.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: It's Sheetmetal and his lot, they all hate me making a racket. And it's not like I'm always itching to say so much. The people here are all too quiet.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Whenever they won't talk, I get so bored, and the only thing I can do is talk to myself for hours on end.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: It used to be that only Grandma Petra would talk with me. And now you too, thank goodness. Oh, no. Do you think I'm annoying as well?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Where I come from, there are many who love speaking more than you do.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: It sounds like a wonderful place!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...It's okay enough.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Where you come from, do the people dance? Just like Grandma Petra was mentioning, dancing in the square?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Occasionally.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Then why haven't I seen you dancing? I've noticed your harp.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Grandma Petra's told me. Don't you all dance around while you sing?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: My dance... none of you may see.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The time, the place, and those before me are all not right.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You're so strange, practically stranger than me. Just where is your home? Are all the people where you're from as strange as you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: (Plucks strings)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Where I'm from, there is no home.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: And I do not know where my home is. My home is long gone.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Well, that's okay. My home was long gone as well, years ago in a gale, when the building collapsed. My mamá was inside when it happened, and she's gone too.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: But that's okay. Everyone's in the same boat. If your house is gone, find another empty one and move in. Plenty of buildings fit the bill here.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: That's right, if you're not happy dancing, then can you sing for me?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: I've never heard anyone else sing before.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Maybe.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Wonderful!

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh, visiting so many places has gotten me hungry.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: You're hungry too, aren't you? If you're hungry, you can't sing, right?

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Let's go find something to eat.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Am I running too fast? I forgot you wouldn't know the way.

steps.name: Female Inhabitant
steps.text: Right, I'm Anita! You can just shout my name from now on, and that way you won't be left behind. Call for me, and I'll stop and wait for you.
